clock_time_reference: The Democracy Clock closed Week 15 at 7:40 p.m., unchanged from the prior week, as the internal ledger moved only 0.3 minutes. This reflects a week of broad but incremental erosion rather than any single sharp break from the preceding pattern.

grand_total_points.note: The net clock movement of 0.3 minutes was small despite wide trait movement, because gains in erosion were partially offset by genuine judicial and civic resistance.

delta_summary.moral_floor: The moral floor continued to erode, with ethics and truthfulness showing the sharpest declines amid pay-to-play access schemes and official amplification of disputed claims.
delta_summary.net_interpretation: The week did not mark acceleration so much as broadening: the same erosive instruments already in use extended into new domains simultaneously, while courts, states, and civil society continued to impose real but only partial friction.

traits_moved.note: Twenty-eight traits registered measurable movement this week, reflecting broad but individually modest shifts across many domains rather than concentration in a few.

long_synopsis: During Week 15, the Democracy Clock held nearly still, moving just 0.3 minutes, even as democratic erosion widened across nearly every domain of governance. Immigration enforcement reached into homes, schools, and mailboxes, deporting citizen children and detaining lawful residents. Courts remained a genuine brake, blocking the Alien Enemies Act and restoring funding, even as a sitting judge was arrested and officials called for more arrests. Universities faced pressure from Washington and turned on their own protesters. Independent journalism lost access and funding while a White House-run outlet rose in its place. Access to power became explicit: a half-million-dollar club, a memecoin dinner, and eighty-nine paused corporate investigations. Congress mostly declined to resist. The clock's stillness reflects not calm but a steadiness of erosion no longer requiring acceleration.
short_synopsis: Week 15 saw erosion spread rather than sharpen: immigration enforcement into homes and mail, judges arrested and attacked, universities squeezed from both sides, media starved while loyal outlets rose, and access to power openly sold, even as courts kept offering real resistance.
